newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vertigo takes edge off German share advance.
newsitem.headline: Vertigo takes edge off German share advance.

text.p: An overnight record high on Wall Street sent German shares within a hair's breadth of new records early on Tuesday, but the surge lost momentum amid nerves at the market's dizzying levels.
"It's just not easy to believe in highs like this," said a Frankfurt trader. "It seems the rise today is mainly on short covering."

The blue chip 30-share DAX index set records for bourse trading at its start but was well off all-time highs set last week during out-of-bourse IBIS electronic dealings and off early highs set in Tuesday's pre-bourse session.
The index was up 10.95 points at 3,586.32 points at 0853 GMT, having tried and failed to vault its alltime record of 3,612.46 points in the IBIS electronic session.
June DTB DAX futures were down 2.5 points at 3,591 points, having earlier shown gains of 25 points.
Some dealers remained confident that the market could regain momentum.
"Everyone felt very good about Wall Street," said another trader. "We should see more records."

One of the pressures on early trade was a slide by Deutsche Telekom AG, partly correcting a recent surge, after the telecommunications giant released 1996 data which confirmed bullish forecasts, but did not surprise, dealers said.
The company posted group net profit of 1.8 billion marks for the year in a report released ahead of its annual news conference later today.
Telekom, which notched up gains of as much as five percent at its height on Monday, was down 84 pfennigs, or two percent, at 40.35 marks in bourse trade.

That was offset by Deutsche Bank AG, traded up 1.65 marks at 96.75 marks, just off an alltime high of 97.75 marks. Dealers attributed its gains to technical factors, aprtly connected to an options expiry deadline on Friday.
Chemical firm Henkel KGaA fell, dropping 1.40 marks to 92.30, after reporting a seven percent rise in pre-tax profit for the first quarter. Dealers also attributed this decline to profit taking.
